acceptanceCriteria.text: `runtime ensure --descriptor` projects the selected release's canonical Route 1 payload identity/locator into the bounded managed-generation reconciliation intent needed by the guest build path.
Guest reconciliation obtains and verifies the exact canonical Route 1 payload bytes by the descriptor-bound SHA-256 before they can enter the Mottainai Nix package build.

The live managed-generation build uses the same canonical payload-consuming package boundary as release Route 2 (`mkMottainaiFromPayload` or one single equivalent authority), not ordinary source-side tarball regeneration.
Route 1 payload SHA-256, Route 2 source NAR SHA-256, and managed-generation identity remain distinct identities with no semantic substitution.
A production-shaped round trip proves that the descriptor-produced canonical `managedGenerationIdentity` is reproduced by the guest/live build path when it consumes the same exact Route 1 payload.
Substituting a different tarball with the same version/source metadata fails closed on payload identity before activation.
Final Route 3 evidence can prove the active Mottainai package is bound to the selected descriptor's canonical Route 1 payload identity, not merely the requested version/source tree.
The fix does not require npm registry publication to precede Route 2/3 convergence and does not create a second package/payload identity authority.
#261's acceptance criterion requiring evidence of the active canonical Route 1 payload can be satisfied without manual payload injection.

issue.title: fix(runtime): consume the release-bound Route 1 payload during guest reconciliation
